property_summary: For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract returns true from supportsInterface when queried for IERC1155MetadataURI.interfaceId (i.e. it reports support for IERC1155MetadataURI) while the mutant fails to report support for IERC1155MetadataURI for that same id (so querying that exact id yields different booleans).

For any account and token id, the reference contract always reverts when balanceOf is called with the zero address (so callers cannot observe a numeric balance for address(0)); the mutant instead returns 0 for address(0), breaking the rule for inputs where account == address(0).

For all addresses and token ids the reference contract always reverts when balanceOf(address(0), id) is called (i.e. querying balanceOf with the zero address is not a successful view), whereas the mutant returns 0 instead of reverting when account == address(0), so there exists an input (account == address(0)) where the mutant does not revert but the reference does.

For all addresses and token ids, calling balanceOf(account,id) on the correct contract never reverts for the zero address but does revert for the contract's own address only in the mutant; the reference allows querying address(0) while the mutant rejects the contract's address causing a divergence for some fuzzed account (account == address(c)).

For any address account and token id, the reference contract's balanceOf(account,id) call never reverts (allows querying address(0) and the contract address), whereas the mutant rejects queries when account == address(c) (reverting), so there exists an account (specifically account == address(c)) for which mutant balanceOf reverts but reference does not.

For every address account and token id, calling balanceOf(account, id) on the reference contract never reverts and returns a uint256; the mutant erroneously reverts when account == address(c) (it disallows querying the contract's own address).

For any address account and token id, the reference contract's balanceOf(account,id) never reverts (it allows querying any account including address(0) and address(c)); the mutant incorrectly reverts when the queried account equals the contract's own address (account == address(c)).

For all addresses and token ids, calling balanceOf(account, id) on the reference C never reverts (it accepts address(0) and the contract's own address); the mutant erroneously reverts when account == address(c) (it forbids querying the contract's own address).

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch returns a uint256[] of the same length where each element equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant that changes the loop to `i <= accounts.length - 1` can under some inputs still return a different array (reads fewer/fails indexing semantics) and thus violate element-wise equality with balanceOf for some indices.

For any accounts and ids arrays of equal length, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) returns an array whose every element at index i equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant's changed loop can produce a differing returned array for some inputs (so the element-wise equality is broken).

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) returns an array where each element equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant's off-by-one loop can produce a returned array that differs (e.g., leaves elements zero) for some inputs.

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) returns an array of the same length whose element at each index i equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant's off-by-one loop can produce a differing returned array for some inputs (it may leave elements unchanged/zero), so this property fails for some fuzzed inputs.

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) returns an array of the same length where every element equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant's changed loop can return a different array for some inputs (it may leave some elements at zero) and thus violates element-wise equality for some fuzzed inputs.

For any input arrays passed to balanceOfBatch where accounts.length == ids.length the reference returns an array whose length equals accounts.length and whose entries are the per-pair balances; the mutant may return an array of length ids.length (different) when ids.length != accounts.length, so the reference always returns an array length equal to the accounts array while the mutant can return a different length for some inputs.

For any inputs, C.balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) returns an array whose length equals accounts.length and each element i equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]); the mutant can return an array sized ids.length when lengths differ, breaking the length equality property for some inputs where accounts.length != ids.length (i.e., the returned array length must equal accounts.length).

For all input arrays, balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) never returns an array whose length differs from accounts.length (the reference always returns length accounts.length and populates index i with balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i])); the mutant can produce a return array with length ids.length when accounts.length != ids.length, breaking this length-equality rule.

For every input arrays (accounts, ids) the reference always returns an array whose length equals accounts.length (and therefore is safe to index up to accounts.length-1); the mutant can return an array of length ids.length when ids.length != accounts.length, violating the length-equals-accounts.length rule for some inputs.

For every input arrays (accounts, ids) the reference C.balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals accounts.length (and each entry i equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i])); the mutant may return an array whose length equals ids.length when ids.length != accounts.length, violating the length-equals-accounts.length rule for some inputs.

For any parallel arrays accounts and ids of equal length, balanceOfBatch never returns a non-zero balance for the zero address (accounts[i] == address(0)) because balanceOf(addr,id) reverts for address(0) in the reference; the mutant bypasses that require and can return a non-zero value for the zero address, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any parallel arrays (accounts, ids) the reference contract always reverts if any accounts[i] == address(0) (so the view call cannot succeed and return a balance for the zero address), whereas the mutant may succeed and return an internal non-zero balance for a zero-address entry — therefore the property: if accounts contains address(0) then balanceOfBatch must revert (reference: always true; mutant: broken for some inputs).

For any parallel arrays (accounts, ids) of equal length where none of the accounts equals address(0), balanceOfBatch returns an array whose i-th entry equals c.balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) (i.e. batch result equals elementwise balanceOf); the mutant can violate this because it reads _balances directly and would return a value for account==address(0) even though balanceOf would revert — so we require inputs with no zero addresses to avoid revert and expose differing return-values when a zero address would otherwise be masked (the fuzzer will find differing elementwise results).

For any parallel arrays accounts and ids of equal length where none of the accounts is the zero address, balanceOfBatch returns an array equal to calling balanceOf on each (i.e. batchBalances[i] == c.balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for all i); the mutant breaks this by reading the internal mapping directly and thus can return a (possibly nonzero) value for address(0) whereas the reference would revert, so ensuring no zero addresses lets the reference always succeed and the mutant sometimes differ.

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays the reference's balanceOfBatch always returns values identical to elementwise calls to balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) (so batchBalances[i] == balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for all i) when every accounts[i] is non-zero; the mutant can differ because it reads the internal mapping directly and can return a value for the zero address entry — so the property enforces all accounts != address(0) and elementwise equality, which holds for the reference for all such inputs but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any equal-length accounts and ids arrays, balanceOfBatch returns per-index ERC1155 balances (batchBalances[i] == balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) for all i); the mutant instead returns prefix sums so this per-index equality is violated for some inputs.
